ns2:section.sectionText: . Wars have been central to the relationship between the United States and Asia and to the history of Asian Americans. This course explores the ways in which twentieth century American wars ø in Asia and elsewhere ø have transformed migrations between Asia and the U.S. as well as warøs impact on Asian Americansø social, economic, political and cultural life. Rather than emphasizing geopolitics, our readings and discussions will focus on themes of migration, citizenship, U.S. imperialism, nationalism and transnationalism, neo- and post-colonialism, and race and racialization. We will trace Asian American histories and experiences through the Philippine-American War, World War II, the Korean War, wars in Southeast Asia, and the post-9/11 period. The broad scope of this course will also allow us to examine such concepts as race, gender, national identity, power and cultural representations.
